title: Neural operators reveal nonreciprocal interactions behind microfluidic nonlinear waves
summary: Interpreting a microfluidic droplet experiment movie with a Fourier neural operator and sparse regression yielded a KdV–Burgers-type continuum model containing a dispersive term absent from the prior Burgers description. The authors’ simulations attribute the nonlinear-wave propagation and stabilization to nonreciprocal hydrodynamic interactions. The work analyzes existing experimental data and does not report a new experiment or a general proof for all nonequilibrium crystals.
ai_technology: Fourier neural operator, interpretable neural-network pipeline and sparse regression
organization: University of Chicago; Old Dominion University; Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1; ENS de Lyon; CNRS

source_review.scope: Primary APS abstract and accepted manuscript for the neural-operator and sparse-regression analysis of microfluidic wave data, affiliation block, source data and publication chronology.

evidence.tested: The authors trained/interpreted a neural-operator network on a microfluidic droplet experiment movie and used sparse regression to derive a KdV–Burgers-type model. The new dispersive term improved the shock-front description relative to Burgers’ equation; a microscopic model attributes nonlinear-wave stabilization/propagation to nonreciprocal hydrodynamic interactions. The source says the model was trained on an existing experimental movie.
evidence.unknown: This is a model-derived interpretation of a specific microfluidic experiment and supporting simulations, not a new experiment or a general proof for all nonequilibrium crystals.
evidence.ai_role: A Fourier neural operator learned latent experimental dynamics from the microfluidic movie; sparse regression extracted the governing equation, and the learned term guided the interpretation of nonreciprocal hydrodynamic interactions.
